items.title: Build the /roadmap build-status page
items.summary: A dependency-free page at /roadmap, backed by data/roadmap.json, that renders one table per status plus in-flight section tables. The living record of work on this project.
items.notes: Exists so work is tracked in one honest place before anything depends on it — storage is a single JSON file the assistant edits directly (no DB, no admin UI, no auth, by design). Kept dependency-free on purpose: no CDN, no build step, so it still opens in five years. Verified the /roadmap route returns 200 and /roadmap.json parses. Observed conflict I did NOT silently resolve: the pasted rules 3-4 (done newest-first, everything else oldest-first as a queue) contradict the follow-up 'order everything newest at the top' — I implemented rules 2-4 as written and flagged it for a ruling rather than quietly picking one. Ruling (2026-08-30): user chose to keep rules 2-4 as the default; header-click sort still overrides per-table (rule 5). Resolved with no code change.

items.title: Wellness Project exercise backfill
items.summary: Flask app finds empty Wellness Project (Health Connect) strength workouts and backfills them from the matching Speediance session's exercises, via an OAuth MCP client. Scheduled daily scan plus a manual button.
items.affects: wellness_client.py, reconcile.py, app.py (/wp/* routes), templates/wp_reconcile.html, tests/
items.notes: Design spec + 9-task TDD plan written and committed (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-30-wellness-project-backfill-design.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-30-wellness-project-backfill.md). Execution: subagent-driven development. Key design finding: Wellness Project exposes no REST API and no API key — its MCP endpoint IS the API, gated by OAuth (authorization_code + PKCE + refresh_token; no machine grant), so the app must connect once in a browser then refresh silently. The date+calories match key was exact across the live 90-day window. Built 2026-08-30 via 9-task subagent-driven development, all tasks reviewed clean and merged to main; automated suite 207 green (2 pre-existing unrelated e2e failures). The independent review gate caught and fixed two real bugs the plan itself had baked in: a CSRF state-expiry bypass (a stale OAuth `state` was still accepted) and a silent SSE data-loss (the MCP parser returned the first `data:` event, so a legal notification-before-result stream yielded an empty result). Two controller rulings: a dedup guard so one Speediance session can't fill two workouts, and a provenance note set directly rather than appending to the Health-Connect note. LIVE SMOKE TEST PASSED 2026-08-31: OAuth connect succeeded end-to-end (token stored 0o600); a real backfill filled Aug-29 'Miami Pull' (WP 696827) with its 5 exercises + provenance note and swept the other empty strength sessions, while the @ Gym and rowing/cardio entries were left untouched — the empty-only + dedup guards held. Observed surprise worth recording: Wellness Project's resolver RENAMES exercises to its own library (e.g. 'Barbell Bent Over Row' -> 'Row [Machine]', 'Seated Barbell Lat Pulldown' -> 'Close Grip Lat Pulldown'); loads and reps are exact, only the names/equipment tags remap. A 'keep literal name' flag is available if verbatim names are wanted later.

items.title: Move Wellness Project backfill into Settings
items.summary: Retire the standalone /wp/reconcile page and surface Connect + Backfill directly in the Settings page's Wellness Project card, with a spinner while a backfill runs.
items.affects: app.py (settings route passes wp_connected; wp_callback + /wp/reconcile redirect to /settings), templates/settings.html, templates/wp_reconcile.html (removed), tests/test_wp_routes.py
items.notes: User found the separate /wp/reconcile page a 'weird empty page' and asked for the controls to live in Settings, plus a spinner during the run. Connect/Backfill move into the existing Wellness Project card; /wp/reconcile and the OAuth callback now redirect to /settings so old links and the redirect_uri still resolve. Done + verified live 2026-08-31: /settings shows Connect when disconnected and a Backfill-now button with an animated spinner + live results panel when connected; /wp/reconcile returns 302→/settings; the OAuth callback lands on /settings; wp_reconcile.html deleted; suite 208 green (2 known-unrelated e2e failures). Results panel and all dynamic text use textContent (no innerHTML), honoring the project XSS rule.

items.title: Backfill: reclassify un-fillable sessions as skipped, not errors
items.summary: Sessions whose Speediance side has no usable data (deleted template, no logged sets) were reported as 'errors', alarming the user. Distinguish 'nothing to backfill here' (skipped) from a real write failure (error).
items.affects: app.py (_apply_match, _run_backfill report buckets), templates/settings.html (result panel), tests/test_wp_backfill.py
items.notes: Found while diagnosing the user's report: 'sync came up with errors instead of pushing today's workout.' Two independent causes. (1) Today's push didn't happen because the run fired before today's Speediance session / its Health-Connect import both existed; a re-run fills it — WP 756813 <-> Speediance 1107027, both 396 cal, exact same-day match. (2) Four old June/July empties genuinely cannot be filled (trainingId with a DELETED template, plus three sessions with no logged sets) and were mislabeled 'errors'. Fix: a per-session 'no usable Speediance data' outcome goes to a new 'skipped' bucket; only a failed WP write counts as an 'error'. The Settings results panel shows Applied / Skipped / Flagged / Errors so recurring un-fillable sessions read as informational, not failures. Done + verified live 2026-08-31: re-run produced applied 1 (today's WP 756813 <- Speediance 1107027, 7 exercises + provenance note), skipped 4 (the deleted-template + no-logged-sets sessions, now labeled SKIP with reasons), errors 0. 3 new tests (empty-detail -> skipped, deleted-template fetch -> skipped, WP-write-failure -> error); suite 211 green.

items.title: Install hourly backfill cron
items.summary: Run the backfill automatically every hour so a day's workout fills without anyone clicking.
items.notes: User asked to run it hourly. Installed in root's crontab at :15 every hour, hitting the loopback port (http://127.0.0.1:5001) directly — that path is behind nginx basic-auth on the public side but open on loopback, so NO password sits in the crontab. flock -n /tmp/wp-backfill.lock makes an overlapping run a no-op; each run appends an ISO timestamp + the JSON result to /var/log/wp-backfill.log. Verified live 2026-08-31: a run logged applied 0 / skipped 4 / errors 0 (today already filled; the 4 un-fillable oldies skipped as designed). The pre-existing 3am cleanup cron was left untouched. Note: the cron is machine state, not in the repo — docs/wp-backfill-cron.md documents the exact line to re-add on a rebuild.

items.title: Mobile hamburger nav
items.summary: The top nav's eight links plus the session indicator overflow on a phone; collapse them into a hamburger menu below the md breakpoint.
items.notes: Desktop (md+) bar is unchanged. Below md the links hide behind a hamburger button that toggles a dropdown; a connection dot stays visible in the bar so signed-in/out status is always glanceable without opening the menu. Nav links are looped from one nav_links list (DRY) rendered in both the desktop bar and the mobile dropdown. Vanilla JS toggle, aria-expanded/aria-controls set for accessibility, hamburger<->X icon swap. Done + verified live 2026-08-31: /settings renders 200 with the desktop bar (hidden md:flex), the md:hidden hamburger, and the mobileMenu dropdown; each nav link appears in both the desktop bar and the dropdown.

items.title: Fix Workout History mobile overflow
items.summary: On phones the History page's header controls ran off the right edge and the records table was clipped. Stack/wrap the header; make the table scroll horizontally.
items.notes: User report: 'the buttons go off screen to the right, and the table is cut off.' Two causes. (1) The header was one non-wrapping 'flex justify-between' row (title + two date inputs + Load/Export/Deep-Export) — now flex-col below the sm breakpoint with the control group flex-wrap, so it stacks and wraps instead of overflowing. (2) The 6-column records table sat in an overflow-hidden wrapper that CLIPPED it; changed to overflow-x-auto and gave the table min-w-[560px] so it scrolls horizontally rather than being cut off or crushed. Verified /history renders 200 with all four responsive classes present. The detail modal was not in scope (user flagged the header buttons + the records table specifically).

items.title: Backfill uses the wrong detail route for Free Lift / Goal-Focused sessions
items.summary: The backfill fetches every non-course session from cttTrainingInfoDetail, which is always empty for Free Lift (type 1/7) and Goal-Focused (type 9) sessions. It should use freeTraining and aiCourseTrainingInfoDetail respectively.
items.affects: app.py (_apply_match), reconcile.py (Free Lift actionList/setList parsing), history detail route
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 while researching other Speediance projects for the MCP server. The three sessions the hourly backfill keeps 'skipping' as 'no loggable exercises' (2874609, 2644826, 2646057) are all Free Lift. Verified live: GET /api/app/trainingInfo/freeTraining/2874609 returns code 0 with actionList = Seated Barbell Row, 3 sets (setList[].summary + rawRepList). The route map comes from pookey/speediance-cli docs/api-notes.md (MIT): type 1/6/7 -> freeTraining, 2 -> courseTrainingInfoDetail, 3/5 -> cttTrainingInfoDetail, 4/9 -> aiCourseTrainingInfoDetail. Caveat before fixing: Free Lift per-set weights carry a 2.2 scale that pookey verified on kg accounts only; this account is lb, so the fix must reconcile against the session's own totalCapacity rather than blindly dividing. Verified live 2026-09-27: deployed, then a backfill run wrote Free Lift 2874609 onto WP 465896 (Seated Barbell Row 3×50 @ 20/25/30 lb). The History page now expands Free Lift, Quick and Goal-Focused sessions (live /api/history/detail checked for 2874609, 3056211, 264945). The other two old 'skipped' Free Lifts are outside the 90-day window; 2646057 also has no exercise picked, so it would be dropped anyway.

items.title: Investigate: does saving a template with presetId <= 0 shrink loads by 2.2?
items.summary: pookey/speediance-cli reports that a non-positive templatePresetId on POST /api/app/v2/customTrainingTemplate makes the server divide every weight and capacity by 2.2. This app sends -1 ('Custom') for movements without an RM preset.
items.notes: UNCONFIRMED for this app — logged so it is not lost. Earlier live checks showed 35 saved = 35 lb, so the app may not be affected (the field names may differ between clients, or the effect may be kg-account-only). Needs one controlled test: save a throwaway template with presetId -1 vs 1, read it back, compare weights. Do not change save logic until that test runs. Hypothesis (2026-09-27): the server treats these fields as POUNDS internally, so the ÷2.2 only bites kg-unit accounts; this account is lb, which would explain the earlier 35 -> 35 lb observation. Same logic applies to the template-level totalCapacity (the app sends the raw set-capacity sum). Still needs the one controlled test before being closed.

items.title: Standalone open-source Speediance MCP server (separate repo)
items.summary: A free, MIT-licensed, self-hostable MCP server replacing GM Manager (going paid): GM Manager's 19 tools plus additions, local stdio mode for Claude Desktop/Code and optional remote OAuth mode for claude.ai. Lives at /srv/speediance-mcp, its own git repo.
items.notes: Design in progress (brainstorming). Decisions so far: Python + official mcp SDK; two phases (core + local stdio first, remote OAuth second); single account per deployment; OAuth login verifies the deployment's own Speediance account; SQLite memory; MIT with hbui3's notice kept; synthetic test fixtures only. Research 2026-09-27: harvested endpoints from stozo04/speediance-cli and pookey/speediance-cli (both MIT); found userinfo/info (profile), freeTraining, aiCourse routes, getHeartRateGraph, and several write faults. Rowing done as a course or custom template has no per-interval data in any known route. Phase 1 BUILT 2026-09-27 on branch phase1 of /srv/speediance-mcp (21 commits, 198 offline tests, all 26 tools, CLI login/logout/status): 14 plan tasks each reviewed, plus a final whole-branch review whose 16 fixes landed (stale token after re-login, non-ASCII Windows timezone header, re-login race, preset-load rebuild guard, load-anchor merge, library download lock). NOT yet verified against the live Speediance account and not merged or published; remaining: merge decision, GitHub repo + push, live acceptance checklist (README), then phase 2 (remote OAuth). Live read-only check 2026-09-27 (reusing the web app's session, no login, no writes): all read tools worked on real data (templates, custom, Free Lift, course rowing with heart rate, Goal-Focused). It found two bugs, logged as #11 and #12, both fixed. Still not live-verified: write tools (create/update/delete/schedule), which need the user's go-ahead.

items.title: MCP bug: bilateral set loads read as half (one cable instead of both)
items.summary: speediance-mcp parsing.set_load took the larger side array for two-sided sets; a barbell set loads both cables, so Barbell RDL templated at 50/60/70 lb read back as 25/30/35. Halved session detail, strength profile, compare and suggest_load (would prescribe half the working weight).
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 in the read-only live check of MCP phase 1 (#10). Evidence: session 1168482 RDL set 1 leftWeights 25s + rightWeights 25s, weights 50s; template weights 50,60,70; userActionStatPage max 70/min 50. Fix: unpinned two-sided set = max(left)+max(right). The web app's history table uses detail.weights for bilateral sets and shows the correct total — not affected. FIXED on branch phase1 (a56be9e) and verified live 2026-09-27: RDL session 1168482 now reads 50/60/70, matching the template; suggest_load bases on 70 lb. Free Lift was checked too and is fine — its set `weight` is already the two-cable total (10 lb per side in rawRepList).

items.title: MCP bug: quick single-exercise sessions (type 7) parse with no exercises
items.summary: speediance-mcp: a type-7 session returned by freeTraining without actionList (e.g. a quick 'Standing Barbell Calf Raise' session) came back with 0 exercises; its sets are only in freeTrainingDetail.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 in the MCP live check (#10): session 3056211 freeTraining dict has no actionList; freeTrainingDetail returns one list-shaped exercise. Fix: fall back to freeTrainingDetail when actionList is empty, shared by session detail and coaching. FIXED on branch phase1 (a3d6269) and verified live 2026-09-27: session 3056211 now parses Standing Barbell Calf Raise, 3 sets 40/45/50 lb, with no cardio/note; strength profile uses the same fallback.

items.title: Hourly WP backfill failing since 2026-08-31: window is 91 days, WP max is 90
items.summary: _wp_window() returns today-90 → today, which list_workouts counts as 91 days; Wellness Project rejects ranges over 90 days, so every scheduled backfill since 2026-08-31 ~15:15 has failed (~600 runs in /var/log/wp-backfill.log).
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 while verifying #8. The last successful run was 2026-08-31 14:15. Our window didn't change, so WP probably started enforcing the 90-day max then. Fix: an inclusive 90-day window (start = today - 89). Verified live 2026-09-27: the backfill connects again (10:39 run: no error).

items.title: Backfill tests overwrite the live wellness_reconcile_report.json
items.summary: tests/test_wp_backfill.py runs the real /wp/backfill route, which writes WP_REPORT_FILE in the app dir, so running the suite replaces the real last-run report (shown in Settings) with fake test data.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27: after a test run the report showed the synthetic sp_training_id 2000001. Fix: tests patch WP_REPORT_FILE to a temp path. The next real run (hourly at :15) overwrites the bad report. Verified live 2026-09-27: a full test run left the real report file untouched (mtime unchanged); the next real run replaced the fake report.

items.title: WP backfill finds no targets: Wellness Project now prints 'kcal' instead of 'cal'
items.summary: reconcile._CAL_RE (\d+\s*cal) doesn't match WP's new '107 kcal' rows, so every workout's calorie parses as None and is_backfill_target rejects all of them. The backfill has had nothing to match against.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 while verifying #8/#13: after fixing the window, the backfill connected but matched nothing. The list row for WP 465896 (2026-07-20, 8 min, empty Health Connect import) reads '· 8 min · 107 kcal'. Fix: accept 'cal' and 'kcal'. Verified live 2026-09-27: the dry run found 6 targets / 5 empty; a live run applied 4 (three custom sessions missed during the outage — 08-31, 09-06, 09-07 — plus the Free Lift) and correctly skipped 1 whose template was deleted.

items.title: Backfilled exercises get fuzzy-matched to the wrong WP exercise/equipment
items.summary: The backfill sends exercise NAMES to WP update_workout; WP resolves them fuzzily. 'Barbell Romanian Deadlift' became 'Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift [Dumbbell (per hand)]' (so its NSI/1RM read 50 lb as per hand) and 'Seated Barbell Row' became 'Seated Cable Row [Cable]'.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 reading back WP 1013643 and 465896 after the #15 backfill. Needs research: whether WP add_exercises accepts an exercise id or equipment hint (list_exercises tool) so we can pin the right movement. Also check earlier backfills for the same mis-mapping. Not guessing a fix.

items.title: MCP login: remember the password by default, --no-remember to opt out
items.summary: speediance-mcp login currently asks 'Remember the password? [y/N]'. Make remembering the default (so expired sessions auto-relogin), drop the prompt, and keep --no-remember for token-only storage.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-27. Trade-off explained to the user: with both the web app and the MCP server remembering the password, each re-login signs the other out (one session per account). Accepted; a shared-session option was offered and not chosen. Done 2026-09-27 on branch phase1 (c157a86): a plain login stores the password with no prompt (tested with input() patched to fail); --no-remember stores only the token; README and spec §15.14 updated; 204 tests pass. Not yet exercised with a real login, since that would sign out the web app's session.

items.title: Speediance session displacement: a new login kills the previous token (code 90 'offline'), whatever the device headers
items.summary: Live test 2026-09-27 (2 logins, user-approved): an Android-identity login killed the web app's token; an iPhone-identity login (different Mobiledevices) then killed the Android token. A displaced token answers code 90 'offline', not 91. Hypothesis that sessions are per device type: REFUTED for Mobiledevices. How GM Manager coexists with the phone is still unknown; a different App_type slot or a partner API are untested.
items.affects: research; web app api_client (code 90 handling); /srv/speediance-mcp client
items.notes: The web app auto-relogins only on 91, so after a phone login it shows 'offline'/signed out until the user clicks Log in, and that manual login is what signs the phone out. My test left the web app on a dead token; restored via /auth/relogin (verified: /api/history works again). Phone signed out as warned. UPDATE 2026-09-27 (user-approved probe): App_type values beyond SOFTWARE exist. WEB needs a request signature (1005 'Signature verification failed'; algorithm not public — not pursued). HARDWARE works with Versioncode '1' (omitting it gives 1003; 41000 gives 1004 'Invalid nonce string'). A byPass login with App_type HARDWARE did NOT kill the SOFTWARE session, and after the user logged into the Android app the HARDWARE session was still alive (code 0) while the web app's SOFTWARE token got 90 'offline'. A HARDWARE-issued token also works on requests sent as SOFTWARE/41000. => Log in as HARDWARE to get a slot that coexists with the phone (likely GM Manager's method). Open risks: HARDWARE may be the Gym Monster's own slot (a HARDWARE login might sign the machine out, unverified); writes and library content not yet tested with a HARDWARE-issued token.

items.title: MCP: treat code 90 'offline' (session taken by another login) as a session loss, not a generic rejection
items.summary: speediance-mcp only treats 91/401 as auth expiry, so when the phone signs in, every tool fails with 'Speediance rejected the request (code 90): offline' and the remembered-password re-login never fires.
items.notes: Found 2026-09-27 in the displacement test. Policy question for the user: on 90, silently re-login (kicks the phone each time Claude is used after the phone) or report 'signed in elsewhere' and wait for an explicit login. Done 2026-09-27 as part of #20 (speediance-mcp fd8eaa2): code 90 now triggers the remembered-password re-login, which is safe now that logins use the HARDWARE slot. Unit-tested.

items.title: Log in as App_type HARDWARE so the web app and MCP server never sign out the phone
items.summary: Use the HARDWARE session slot (found in #18) for logins in the web app and speediance-mcp, keeping every other request as SOFTWARE/41000; treat code 90 as a session loss and silently re-login.
items.notes: Requested 2026-09-27. The user couldn't check whether the Gym Monster stayed signed in after the HARDWARE test login and said to assume it's OK — watch for the machine being signed out. Supersedes #19 (code 90 handling). Web app deployed 2026-09-27 (merged feat/hardware-session): after /auth/relogin with the HARDWARE login, verified live history list, session detail, exercise detail, and a throwaway template create → read back (Barbell Bent Over Row 5 @ 10) → delete. MCP on phase1 (fd8eaa2), tests pass. Still waiting for the user to confirm the Android app stayed signed in after the web app's HARDWARE re-login. VERIFIED 2026-09-27: the user confirmed the Android app was still signed in after the web app's HARDWARE re-login. Gym Monster status unverified (user not at the machine) — watch for it.
